judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short interpretive note that masculine terms include all employees; the wording is plain and creates no operative right to argue about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It harmonises with the pervasive use of 'men'/'he' throughout (e.g., 2-L.2, 4-A.3) rather than conflicting with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard recital of parties; 'or its successor' is slightly open-ended but the sentence is otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 says the agreement is to be treated as an individual agreement between the Union and each Publisher, which sits in mild tension with the Association-as-agent framing here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A radius of approximately fifty miles' and a boundary 'bounded approximately as follows' are self-consciously imprecise, and the listed towns may not match a 50-mile radius.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Metropolitan Area definition is relied on by 2-E.1, 2-E.2(e), 3-E, 3-F and 21-D(V), so a boundary dispute would ripple, but no provision contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recognition clause is a long enumerated list of job categories, exactly the kind of list whose outer edge (what counts as a covered 'operation') invites expressio unius argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-B extends coverage to 'any other operation ... now being performed exclusively' by unit employees, and 2-C and 22-A jurisdiction minutes all bear on the same boundary; contribution duties in 13-H/13-I key off 'employees in the bargaining unit'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the same manner as present practice', 'other government or municipal building' after a specific list, and the parenthetical definition of 'dealer' are all genuinely open-textured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 3-B (Publisher decides manner of wrap/tie and number of dealers) and 2-A.1 routemen jurisdiction, but no direct contradiction is apparent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A residual catch-all ('any other operation, occupation or branch of work') qualified by 'now being performed exclusively' — a classic general-versus-specific scope problem against the 2-A.1 list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 2-A.1, 2-C and 2-H.1 (which freezes existing mailroom jurisdiction among several unions), the reach of the residual clause is genuinely contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'New mechanical devices' introduced to 'perform or aid in the performance of' unit operations is broad and its edge is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pulls against 3-D.4/3-D.5 on automation (which contemplate automation displacing situations) and against 2-H.1 preserving other unions' mailroom jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat recognition of named terminal types as delivery points; the language is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-E.1 (buses/ferries/airplanes) and 22-C(b) airport pickup; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Where for any reason distribution is interrupted' is broad but the operative permission is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with 3-C (Canada point men) and 2-A.1 'Canada men' without tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Existing means or methods', 'good cause shown', and the closing saving clause about substituting 'for a bus or railroad now being used' pull against the opening prohibition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 2-E.2(h) (Publisher may at any time employ railroad, aircraft or any other form of transportation) which appears to cut against this restriction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line permission that employees may be required to operate tractor-trailers; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D expressly reinterprets Section 2-E.2 for The Times, but as to (a) there is no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cross-reference to Section 4-B is odd since 4-B deals with filling vacant situations rather than driver selection, and 'qualified, in order of seniority' could be read two ways.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B governs vacancies by 'qualification and competence' and seniority; the cross-reference is at least imprecise against that section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable number of employees' is an undefined quantity, though the obligation is otherwise modest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision fixes the number or the training obligation; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This article is intended only to establish terms and conditions' plus 'free to select any runs' is a management-rights statement whose interaction with the mandatory (e) is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits directly against 2-E.2(e) requiring unit drivers to transfer points and 22-D Point Two which rewrites (e) for The Times.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To be agreed upon by the parties' and 'as near the limits of such areas as practical' are indefinite, with a fallback to the Impartial Chairman.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D expressly reconstrues paragraph (e) for The Times with mileage rules, creating a two-track regime that must be reconciled with this text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear rule that Albany-type runs are driven through by unit employees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D(i) excepts runs beyond 250 miles or with more than two stops for The Times, which qualifies this apparently absolute rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Presently recognized exchange points' is undefined and the text is OCR-mangled, but the mechanism is describable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with (g) and (h) and with 22-D; no direct contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Jurisdictional dispute with another union resulting from the operation of this article' is a broad trigger for a unilateral right to discontinue runs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels 9-B and 22-D(vii) which use similar jurisdictional-dispute escape hatches; no contradiction, though it sits against 2-E.2(e)'s mandatory language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other form of transportation provided for by this contract to the extent that such forms ... may now be employed' is circular and hard to bound.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in visible tension with 2-E.1's prohibition on substituting buses, ferries or airplanes for existing means, and 22-D(x) expressly stipulates limits on (h) for The Times.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Laid off solely as a result of' is a causation standard that can be gamed, but the sentence is short and clear in aim.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.1 recognises an unlimited right to lay off for economic or business reasons, so 'solely as a result' is the only thing separating the two rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar bonus per shift; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 3-Q hi-lo bonus and 13-A wage schedules; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single conditional prohibition on contracting with another union as to inspectors and Return Department employees; the language is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-H.1 preserves other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, which is a related but not contradictory subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice, however, excepted' is an unbounded carve-out swallowing the rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same 'present practice' device appears in 3-G, 12-C and 5-N; here it undercuts the tying jurisdiction otherwise given by 2-A.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conditions and methods of operation now prevailing ... shall not be disturbed' is vague, and the arbitration duty is conditioned on 'provided such other union or unions agree'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is in tension with 2-A/2-B/2-C jurisdictional grants and with 2-H.2 extending Union jurisdiction to new buildings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fairly clear: jurisdiction in a new annex or building is as defined in 2-A and 2-B; 'full operations commence' is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on 2-A/2-B scope and sits against 2-H.1's freeze of prevailing mailroom conditions — a genuine reconciliation question for a new plant like Carlstadt (22-A).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A double-negative sentence with garbled text, but the protective rule against discharge for inability to do other work is discernible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Reconcilable with 4-A.4 (no employment or promotion unless qualified) and 14-A discharge for cause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is missing a verb ('entitled to for work'), which obscures the very right created — a mechanical defect going to meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The shape/hiring machinery in 4-A.2 governs who may work, so the 'right herein created' has to be read against that scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short prohibition with an express foreman exception; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-B limits foremen from performing Section 2 operations beyond a regular shift, which complements rather than contradicts this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Maximum Union security permissible under the Labor Management Relations Act ... to the extent embodied in Section 17' is a self-referential and legally contingent formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-A prints the old closed-shop 2-L in italics as not part of the Agreement yet provides it revives automatically if the law changes, which sits awkwardly with this operative clause and with 2-L.2's 30-day membership rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 30-day union-membership rule for regular situation holders.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Must be read with 2-L.1 and 17-A's suspended closed-shop text and 2-N.3's agency fee for non-members, which together raise a coherence question about non-member status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading 'Work on Sixth Shift' does not match the text, the opening line is garbled, and 'the full shift' vs 'in excess of a fifth shift' is ambiguous as to what is paid at time and one-half.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical sentence appears in the italicised, non-operative 2-L reproduced in 17-A.1, so the same words appear both as operative and as excluded text.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One flat prohibition on engaging helpers; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 10 half-day boys work 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man', which is at least an apparent counterpoint to this ban.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed, mechanical check-off procedure with definite timing; low interpretive surface.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A side letter permits amendment to weekly or bi-weekly checkoff on 60 days' notice, which modifies but does not contradict this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statutory-compliance sentence; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels 17-B's separability clause; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mechanics with a percentage cap; the only softness is the 5%-of-monthly-dues cap applied to a per-shift amount.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-L.2 requires membership of regular situation holders, so agency fees apply only to extras and casuals — consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The schedules shown in the last notice of such schedules' is an external, undocumented reference, though the 46-pound cap is hard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-H sets Times bundle schedules with weights up to 46 pounds and 21-C.2/21-D set News load maxima, which must be squared with this general clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires publication of a schedule; language is administrative and definite apart from OCR noise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D and 22-H fix specific load and tailman schedules for the two shops, which supplement rather than contradict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A posting requirement; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-G posting of lists; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unduly burdensome' and 'newspaper operational conditions warrant it' are vague standards, but they are referred to arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Routes complaints to Section 16, consistent with 3-B and 16-A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unduly burdensome' and 'unduly difficult to serve' are open standards paired with a broad management right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 2-A.2 (wrapper made up by a unit member) and 3-H.1 (no excessive work tasks) without direct contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Personally supply all dealers and newsboys' is short and concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 2-D.2 Canada points; nothing else touches it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Economic or business reasons' and 'as such Publisher may find necessary or desirable' are broad, though 3-D.2 supplies a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 2-E.2(i), 2-A.2 and 20-E.6 no-layoff guarantees and against 5-G's duty to maintain as many situations as possible — a real harmonisation problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional clause that expressly disclaims prior practice; it broadens rather than narrows, but its 'usual and ordinary sense' formula is itself indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the interpretive key to 3-D.1 and 16-M.3's layoff exception; consistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The re-employment duty and the 'shall in no way limit the Publisher's right to lay off' proviso point in opposite directions within one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to 'Section 3-D' generally and disclaims effect on 3-E/3-F methods-and-extent clauses, which is exactly where reconciliation is difficult.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list of automated systems is introduced by 'shall be construed to include, among other such ... systems', a general-plus-specific formulation whose reach (e.g., satellite transmission) is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The May 1, 1981 list versus the 'after May 1, 1965' installation date is internally awkward and interacts with 3-D.1's unrestricted economic layoff right and 3-D.6's savings clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but mechanical; the phrase 'shall remain employed as regular situation holders, but their regular situations shall be bid for' is convoluted yet workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on 4-B bidding procedure and 3-D.4's list; the interaction with 20-E's excess-situation-holder scheme is a possible source of overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings clause stacking multiple 'nor ... nor' qualifications; hard to read but each limb is identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly tries to reconcile 5-G, 3-D.1 and Section 16, which is itself an acknowledgment that those provisions pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Methods and extent ... as they exist ... at the time of the effective date' freezes an undocumented status quo, an inherently vague benchmark.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-F frees the Publisher to choose delivery form for new sections or routes and 3-D.3 disclaims modification of this clause; the boundary between 'existing' and 'new' is a live issue, and a side letter on 'Clarification of Method and Extent' addresses subcontracting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'New sections or new routes' is an undefined category on which the whole freedom turns.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express exception to 3-E's freeze, so the two provisions define each other's edges and can be read inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practices' and 'good cause shown' are vague but standard here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is duplicated almost verbatim by 12-C, raising a redundancy rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Undue hardship or hazard', 'excessive work tasks' and 'insofar as practicable' are classic vague standards, though referred to the Board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A side letter on heaters, Bostrum seats and safety equipment supplements this; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '$20,000, $50,000 beginning January 1, 1982' is elliptical and the coverage trigger ('for damages arising out of injuries or death resulting from assaults or other criminal conduct') is a general-after-specific formulation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7-F and 13-B.2 deal with workers' compensation benefits separately; no direct conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear management right paired with a pay obligation keyed to the shift scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 5-A/5-B define the shifts and 13-A fixes the rates, so it fits the scheme; 6-C requires supervision on such shifts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Every effort', 'in so far as that may be practicable' and the two disclaimers make the obligation nearly self-cancelling.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-I pays double time for Sunday advance-section work, so the overtime-avoidance duty here interacts with, but does not contradict, that premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Then fair value' and 'no longer is fit for use' are soft, and the anti-discrimination proviso is open-ended, but the structure is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grandfathering of existing employee-owned equipment against the flat opening prohibition is an internal tension resolved on the face of the clause itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly mangled and the two sentences appear to conflict: matter handled 'as the Publisher may direct' versus matter that 'shall be tied, handled and delivered by an extra crew'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D(V)(c) expressly disapplies the 3-L extra-crew requirement to Newspoint commercial work, showing the clause's reach was itself contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An extremely long single-sentence most-favoured-terms clause with a break in the middle ('at any time thereafter on written notice to the Union. to make effective'), obscuring the condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the side letters granting the Union any better pension/welfare terms given other unions; no contradiction, but the interaction with 12-A wholesaler agreements is arguable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list ('articles of association, constitution, charter, by-laws, codes, laws, regulations, resolutions or rules of any character') followed by a general catch-all; scope of 'of any character' is loose but the rule is simple.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-B (separability for legal conflicts) and 17-C (spirit and letter) cover adjacent ground consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best efforts ... to promote the business and interests of the several Publishers' is a paradigmatically vague obligation with no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits oddly beside 16-N's no-strike clause and 3-M's restrictions, but nothing directly contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The immediate-family list is enumerated then extended by 'and legal dependents as defined by the Internal Revenue Code', a specific-plus-general formulation; the 'provided such three days fall within the regularly scheduled work-week' proviso is also a limiting condition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-K paid leave and 7-A holidays cover overlapping absences but do not conflict with this.
